subject: AWS Marketplace: SaaS metering & entitlement onboarding plan
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: AWS Marketplace PM <aws-marketplace-pm@amazon.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-10-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: AWS Marketplace: SaaS metering & entitlement onboarding plan

Sarah —

Thanks again for taking a look at our Marketplace listing. Per our call earlier, I put together a short onboarding plan to get Acme onto AWS Marketplace SaaS (metering + entitlement) without blocking your procurement timeline. High level:

- Confirm contract vehicle (SaaS Contract via AWS Seller Console + Private Offer if needed).
- Map entitlements to metering dimensions (monthly active users = "MAU", seats, or API calls).
- Decide fulfillment method (SaaS contract + Marketplace entitlement check via API).
- Sign SaaS addendum and upload to Seller Console.

Attached: redwood_aws_ma_pricing_matrix.xlsx (pricing bands we recommend) and a draft entitlement map.

Questions for you:
1) Which metering dimension does Acme prefer — MAU or seat-based?
2) Is procurement expecting a Private Offer (negotiated price) or standard AWS Marketplace listing?
3) Do you require Redwood to accept any specific data residency/KMS language in the addendum?

Proposed next steps:
- You confirm metering dimension and Private Offer preference (by Wed 10/27).
- We share final entitlement mapping and create a draft Private Offer if requested.
- AWS PM on this thread will kick off onboarding flow (Seller Console steps + entitlement testing).

If you want, I can set up a dedicated enablement call next week to walk the Acme engineering and procurement teams through the flow.

Thanks —
Sean Gallagher
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0142

Attachments: redwood_aws_ma_pricing_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), mismatch_entitlement_map.csv (CSV)

From: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acme-cloud.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: AWS Marketplace PM <aws-marketplace-pm@amazon.com>, Acme Cloud Legal <legal@acme-cloud.com>
Date: 2026-10-22T11:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace: SaaS metering & entitlement onboarding plan

Sean —

Thanks for the clear outline and the attachments. A few quick answers and asks from Acme:

- Metering: we prefer a MAU model with monthly reconciliation. We expect a spike to ~120k MAUs in month 1 for onboarding tests, then steady-state ~25k MAU.
- Offer type: Procurement prefers a Private Offer so we can lock pricing for 12 months, but they need to see the SaaS addendum and any KMS language first.
- Compliance: our security team will need to validate that entitlements checks do not transmit customer PII to third parties. Can you confirm Redwood's entitlement API only exchanges opaque account IDs?

Also: can you confirm timeline if we sign the addendum this week? Procurement is pushing for go-live by 11/15.

Thanks —
Sarah Li
Head of Cloud Platform, Acme Cloud
sarah.li@acme-cloud.com

From: AWS Marketplace PM <aws-marketplace-pm@amazon.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com>, Sarah Li <sarah.li@acme-cloud.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-10-23T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace: SaaS metering & entitlement onboarding plan

Hi all —

Quick note from the Marketplace side on the mechanics and timeline:

1) Metering dimension: MAU is a common dimension; implementers typically call our Metering Service with (CustomerAccountId, Dimension="MAU", Quantity). That will support monthly aggregation and billing.
2) Private Offer: Seller (Redwood) must create the Private Offer in the Seller Console and reference the Buyer account; once created, Buyer accepts and Marketplace handles invoicing. Private Offer creation can be done in parallel with entitlement testing.
3) Entitlement checks: when a customer calls Redwood, Redwood must call the Marketplace Entitlement API with the Buyer’s AWS Account ID (not PII). We recommend mapping Acme accounts to their AWS Account IDs in your entitlement table.
4) Onboarding checklist:
   - Upload the signed SaaS addendum to the Seller Console.
   - Provide a test Buyer AWS Account ID for entitlement verification.
   - Provide a sandbox API key and a test MAU payload so we can validate meter ingestion.

Timeline: with documents signed and test Buyer account in hand, we can complete validation in 5 business days. That supports a go-live by 11/15 if sign-off happens by 11/02.

I'll follow up with a Seller Console checklist link and a short runbook for entitlement call patterns.

— AWS Marketplace PM

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: PrIyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.inference.com>, AWS Marketplace PM <aws-marketplace-pm@amazon.com>
Date: 2026-10-26T10:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace: SaaS metering & entitlement onboarding plan

Sean / Karthik —

Legal has a couple of redlines on the SaaS addendum: operator liability cap adjusted, explicit KMS integration clause requested, and clarification on data retention for marketplace logs. I attached mismatch_entitlement_map.csv which flags the current mapping where Acme expects MAU per-tenant while our billing tiers are per-customer. We need to reconcile before creating the Private Offer.

Can we do a 30-min alignment call with Acme legal and engineering Thursday 10/28 or Friday 10/29? I'll own the addendum edits and circulate an updated PDF for signature.

Also, Karthik — please prepare:
- a one-page doc showing how our entitlement lookup uses AWS Account ID only (no emails or PII),
- a test payload sample for MAU ingestion.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Director, Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com

Attachment: mismatch_entitlement_map.csv

From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sarah Li <sarah.li@acme-cloud.com>, AWS Marketplace PM <aws-marketplace-pm@amazon.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2026-11-02T15:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: AWS Marketplace: SaaS metering & entitlement onboarding plan

Team —

Thanks for the quick reviews. Consolidating into an agreed mutual action plan so we have one source of truth:

MUTUAL ACTION PLAN (high level):
1) 11/02 - Redwood circulates updated SaaS addendum with KMS clause (Marissa) — DONE.
2) 11/03 - Acme legal to review & sign addendum (Sarah / Acme Legal).
3) 11/03 - Acme sends a test AWS Account ID for entitlement verification (Sarah).
4) 11/04 - Karthik shares entitlement one-pager + sample MAU payload (Karthik).
5) 11/05-11/09 - AWS validation window (AWS Marketplace PM).
6) 11/10 - Private Offer created by Redwood and sent to Acme for acceptance.
7) 11/15 - Go-live target (billing through AWS).

Action items assigned in HubSpot: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/7542 (I added due dates and owners). Please confirm the 11/03 sign & test-account commitment so we can hit 11/15.

Notes / clarifications:
- Entitlement API will only receive Buyer AWS Account IDs. We will not send emails or other PII (per Karthik’s one-pager).
- MAU spike guidance: we will configure initial rate limits for ingestion and enable burst capacity for onboarding month 1.
- Attachments for procurement: signed_saas_addendum.pdf will be uploaded to the Seller Console after signature; Private Offer requires Buyer account ID and price matrix (see attached spreadsheet).

I'll coordinate the enablement call once Acme confirms the 11/03 items. Thanks everyone for moving fast on this.

Best —
Sean Gallagher
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.inference.com
+1 (415) 555-0142
